findings.evidence: OpenCode runs behind bubblewrap filesystem isolation with private runtime path variables removed; only the disposable workspace, credential home, and read-only system runtime are mounted.
Provider-owned Git metadata is never used for publication; model output is mirrored into a fresh parent-owned publisher clone with canonical repository binding and force-with-lease publication.
Primary checkout synchronization compares HEAD to head_before before and after fetch and refuses destructive reset on concurrent advancement.
Targeted validation uses the fallback runtime working directory and a credential-free pinned GitHub origin, so the validation env allowlist does not need repository path/binding variables.

The publisher now runs the repository-owned pre-push boundary before remote mutation, then exact-head targeted validation before primary checkout sync; failed post-push validation force-with-lease restores the exact prior remote head.

Provider-result commits are created with the canonical fafa33 writer identity, explicit git -S signing, verify-commit proof, and publication no longer bypasses the repository pre-push provenance boundary.

OperationalAgentFallbackRuntime now injects the trusted OpenCode adapter bindings for Evidence DB, repository identity, authenticated publication, executable/model and sandbox configuration independently of the optional provider allowlist; the model process still strips those private/credential variables.
